title: 50 First Dates
sub: Two clocks: what the film shows you, and what actually happens.
notes: The loop is the film's whole idea: Lucy wakes each morning with no memory, so the same first date happens again and again. Real time stops moving; the running order keeps going.

How the repeats are numbered: the three repeat mornings get 7, 8 and 9 on the real spine, in the order the film shows them (labelled Morning 1, 2, 3). The format forbids two scenes sharing a position, so one held morning takes three consecutive slots — read that band as a single point in real time.

The two backward cuts are the film's own: the family's staged morning (shown mid-flow) has actually been running since just after the crash a year before, and the crash tape that explains Lucy is the oldest thing in the film, screened near the end.
Real time only resumes at the journal, the boat and the coda — the three places where the two clocks start running together again.
Chronology is a judgement call only for the ritual: it sits at its origin, a year before the present, because the reveal is that this same morning has been restaged every day since.
legend_note: Node numbering: left spine = screening position, right spine = real order. Where the repeat mornings run straight and parallel, real time is standing still.
